title: Section 6: graceful drain loop subscribe-before-check is correct
description: main.rs:344-355 registers Notify::notified() BEFORE loading the in_flight counter, then awaits if the counter is nonzero. This is the correct ordering for a notify-based drain loop: if the last connection calls notify_one() between the load and the await, the notification is already queued and notified.await returns immediately. Reversing the order (load first, then register notified) would introduce a race where the notification is missed, causing the drain to hang. A contributor doing a 'cleanup' refactor might flip the order — this comment defends the current ordering.
